subject.title: [Bug]: Telegram slash sessions still resolve to channel=(unknown), causing elevated allowFrom checks to fail on 2026.3.13

question: Which repair should own Telegram slash-session channel recovery for elevated allowFrom without broadening the elevated authorization boundary?
rationale: The bug is source-visible, but the fix touches session identity used by elevated host-command authorization, and the open linked fork PRs differ in scope and proof.

options.title: Adopt a narrow scoped-key repair
options.body: Use the safer shape from the mergeable fork candidate or an equivalent fresh patch, add a regression test for `telegram:slash:<id>`, and require redacted live Telegram proof before closing this issue.

options.title: Broaden runtime channel inference
options.body: Add a shared runtime/session-key channel inference helper only if maintainers want the same fallback to cover sandbox explain and elevated runtime paths beyond Telegram slash diagnostics.

options.title: Defer until live repro is available
options.body: Keep the issue open without adopting a fix until a maintainer or contributor supplies an end-to-end Telegram elevated run proving the runtime half of the report.

recommendation.title: Adopt a narrow scoped-key repair
recommendation.body: Use the safer shape from the mergeable fork candidate or an equivalent fresh patch, add a regression test for `telegram:slash:<id>`, and require redacted live Telegram proof before closing this issue.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent current-main history shows the broadest ownership signal across sandbox explain, session metadata, and directive/elevated-adjacent paths.
